zh: 细读巴门尼德——本体论之父，因而也是我们数世纪以来所知的（欧洲）

哲学之父——提出的公设，便会发现：西方理性思想诞生之初提出的谜题从未真正解决。芝诺悖论至今仍是悖论——对哲学而言更是如此，而非对科学——而“无中不能生有”在今日仍是物理—形而上学定律，一如它在公元前六、五世纪的欧洲文明中那样。前苏格拉底哲学家接受这一原则；甚至那些主张变化与运动可能的人，如原子论者，也必须设法绕过它，而不是挑战它。在埃利亚学派体系中——直到亚里士多德都未受挑战——“无中不能生有”意味着：变化不可能，虚空不存在，万物始终以坚实不变的形式存在。“虚空”在本体论意义上意味着虚无；而运动则意味着本体论意义上的“生成”，这一论述诉诸的是本体论，而不是自然哲学。运动被理解为成为一个“ousia”（本质或实体），这与“本质具有不可毁灭的永恒性质——因此始终已经存在”这一原则相矛盾。变化的观念违反了埃利亚学派的基本前提，即其公理中的公理：无不存在，虚无不存在，而“成为”将意味着占据先前“空”的（虚无的）空间。在巴门尼德那里，绝对意义上的虚无、非存在与虚空被等同起来，并在整个古代一直如此；不过也有一些例外，即直接与这种逻辑对抗的例子，我们将在本书后面讨论。至于原子论者，他们找到了一种弯曲巴门尼德规则的方法，而不是挑战或反驳它。
en: A close reading of the postulates put forward by Parmenides – the father of ontology and thus of (European)

philosophy as we have known it for centuries – discloses the fact that the riddles posed at the birth of Western rational thought have never been resolved. Zeno’s paradox is still a paradox – more so to philosophy than to the sciences – and ‘nothing comes from nothing’ is as much of a physical-metaphysical law nowadays as it was in sixth and fifth century BC of the European civilization. The principle was accepted by the pre-Socratics, and even those who advocated that change and movement were possible, such as the atomists, had to find a way around it instead of challenging it. In the Eleatic system, unchallenged till Aristotle, ‘nothing comes from nothing’ meant: change was impossible, empty space didn’t exist and everything had always existed in solid and unchangeable form. ‘Empty space’ meant nothingness in the ontological sense, whereas movement implied coming into being in the ontological sense argued in terms of ontology instead of physical philosophy. Movement was taken to be becoming an ousia, an essence or substance, which contradicts the principle that essence is of indestructible everlasting nature – and has, thus, always already existed. Nothingness, non-being and empty space (or void) in the absolute sense are equated in Parmenides and continue to be so throughout antiquity, with some exceptional examples of direct confrontation with this logic that we will discuss further in this book. As for the atomist approach, it found a way to bend the Parmenidean rule rather than challenge or refute it.

zh: 因此，后来几个世纪的自然哲学和科学所处理的空间范畴，既缺席于巴门尼德的推理，也缺席于古希腊那些反对他但从未挑战该原则及其等式的人——即“虚空等于本体论意义上的虚无”（意译）。最早挑战这一公设的，且仍是罕见例子的，是亚里士多德；他基于该公设本身的性质或本质提出质疑：每个谓词都与某种“某物”相关（希腊语ousia 即to ti，意为“某物”或“什么”）。此外，ousia 概念植根于多样性；按照亚里士多德的范畴体系，存在（to on）并非只有一种ousia。

zh: 虚空作为运动的先决条件

children: Empty space as a precondition of movement

zh: 从巴门尼德到晚期原子论者——以及在与教条有显著偏离时包括亚里士多德——乃至整个古代，要产生运动，就必须存在未被任何程度实体填充或占据的虚空。无论是“（某）物”（to ti）这一物理概念，还是诸如toon——即存在，或任何形式的实体/本质/同一性（ousia）——这样的本体论概念，对古代思想家而言，运动不过是某物或某实体出现在此前空无一物的场所的一种表象：“因为虚空就是无”［原文：τὸ γὰρ κενεὸν οὐδέν ἐστιν］，梅利索斯说（DK 30B7.7）。

即使空间只在极短瞬间被（绝对地）“清空”，虚无的可能性——进而虚空的可能性——也被允许。这被视为违反巴门尼德法则“无中不能生有”。这种可能性会与最高真理、最纯粹的同一反复相矛盾——“无中不能生有”，或者说“存在即存在，不能是非存在”——这似乎在古代哲学中被普遍接受，即使像亚里士多德那样对其提出质疑。变化也是运动，因为它涉及成为、生成和产生，因此是某种本质上显然不在的东西的产生。对变化——进而对成为或生成——的严格巴门尼德式反对是：如果“无中不能生有”，那么存在（to on）或ousia 已经以其绝对形式存在，因此成为被排除。于是万物始终如其所是地存在，不变、不动、坚实——不允许任何虚空或虚无的裂缝。此外，万物不朽——某物不能转化为无，因为无不能成为某物。变化只是幻象；可见世界是幻象、梦境、幻觉，正如苏格拉底在临终时所解释的（柏拉图，66e–67a）。
这种观点一直作为主导观点延续到新柏拉图主义、中世纪哲学，以及更近期的“新理性主义”对理性——即科学思维——的迷恋，与威尔弗里德·塞拉斯所说的“现实的显现图景”相对。（我们这里指对塞拉斯的一种特定接受
，而不是他本人承认“民间推理”与科学思维连续性的著作。

）哲学的诞生、存在概念的诞生以及完全理性思维（同一反复）的诞生，恰与一种世界观同时诞生：它宣称直接经验的现实是幻象。它也恰与“身体恐惧症”的诞生同时发生，因为真理不可能也不存在于腐朽肉体的可见世界中，而存在于完美、不可见、没有任何身体或物质的世界中（柏拉图，《斐多篇》，64c–65c）。让我们考察巴门尼德论证的诸范畴，它们标记了数世纪乃至数千年的唯心主义和反唯物主义，并看看它们如何形成一个界定明确、不可穿透的立场。
en: From Parmenides to the late atomists – and, with a significant aberration from the dogma, through Aristotle – as well as throughout antiquity, for there to be movement, there has to be empty space not filled with or occupied by a body of any sort of degree. Be it a physical notion of a ‘(some)thing’ (tò tí) or an ontological concept such as
– that is, the Being or substance/essence/identity of any sort (

) – to the Ancient thinkers, movement is simply an appearance of a thing or an entity at a place where there was nothing prior to it: ‘for the empty is nothing’ [in the original: τὸ γὰρ κενεὸν οὐδέν ἐστιν], argues Melissus (DK 30B7.7).

Even if the space is ‘vacated’ (in an absolute way) for only an infinitesimally short moment of time, the possibility of nothingness, and thus empty space, is allowed. This is considered a breach of the Parmenidean law ‘nothing comes from nothing’. Such a possibility would contradict the utmost truth, the purest tautology of them all – nothing comes from nothing, or, being is being and cannot be not-being – that seems to be universally accepted in ancient philosophy even when problematized, for example, by Aristotle. Change is movement too,

en: , and thus coming to being of something which is apparently not in its essence. A strictly Parmenidean objection to change, and thus to becoming or generation, would be that if nothing comes from nothing, the being (

is already there in its absolute form, and thus becoming is precluded. Everything, therefore, has always existed as it ever was, unchanged, unmoving, solid – no crack of empty space or nothingness is allowed. Also, everything is undying – something cannot be transformed into nothing since nothing cannot become something. Change is but an illusion; the visible world is an illusion, a dream, a hallucination, as Socrates explains at his deathbed (Plato, 66e–67a).

This view has persisted as the dominant one well into Neoplatonism, medieval philosophy and, more recently, in the neorationalist fetishizing of rationality, that is, of scientific thought as opposed to ‘the manifest image of reality’ as per Wilfrid Sellars. (We are referring here to a particular reception of Sellars
rather than his own writings that admit continuity between ‘folk reasoning’ and scientific thought.

) The birth of philosophy, of the notion of being and of perfectly rational thought (tautology) coincides with the birth of a world view that declares the immediately experienced reality an illusion. It coincides with the birth of somatophobia too, as the truth cannot and does not lie in the visible world of rotting flesh but in the perfect, invisible world without bodies or matter of any sort (Plato,

, 64c–65c). Let us consider the categories of the Parmenidean arguments that have marked centuries and millennia of idealism and anti-materialism and how they form a perfectly circumscribed and impenetrable position.

zh: “无中不能生有”这一原则至今有效：其科学与哲学本体论阐释

children: Nothing comes from nothing, a principle that is valid to this date: Scientific and philosophical-ontological accounts of it

zh: 迄今为止，从牛顿到霍金，这一原则——“无中不能生有”——似乎在科学中未受质疑。哲学似乎允许更多可能：随着启蒙运动后的思想变革，哲学越来越成为独立于科学的沉思散文，也就越来越允许自相矛盾的立场和与科学直接矛盾的观点。因此，“无中不能生有”在现代哲学中并不必然是普遍共识。虚无本身似乎也是一种存在；根据某些哲学家的说法，它在本体论上存在，尤其在现代性开始之后；试看存在主义、虚无主义以及黑格尔的非存在概念。
en: To this date, from Newton to Hawkins, this principle – ‘nothing comes from nothing’ – seems undisputed by the sciences. It seems that philosophy has allowed for more possibilities: the more it has become meditational prose, independent of the sciences following the intellectual overhaul of the Enlightenment, the more paradoxical positions and those in direct contradiction with science have been permitted. Thus, ‘nothing comes from nothing’ is not necessarily a matter of universal consensus for modern philosophy. Nothingness in its own right is also being, it seems,and it is ontologically existent according to some philosophers, in particular with the beginning of modernity; consider existentialism, nihilism and Hegel’s notion of non-being.

zh: 这种对科学讨论的漠视和对经验材料的蔑视，表明本章导言中所述的定义希腊哲学的“可见”与“不可见”、有形与无形、物质与观念之间的原始二分仍在延续。柏拉图认为可见世界是幻象，经验记录不足以对存在作出合理说明，至少不能被视为绝对。
en: This absence of heed for the scientific discussions and contempt for the empirical point to the continuation of the originary division between the ‘visible’ and ‘invisible’, bodily and incorporeal and physical and ideal defining Greek philosophy, as noted in the introduction to this chapter. Plato argued that the visible world is an illusion and that the empirical record does not amount to a viable account of making sense of being, at least not one seen as an absolute.

zh: 哲学从古至今一直以人类为中心：马克思在《对黑格尔哲学的总体批判》（收录于《1844 年经济哲学手稿》）中阐明，所谓的绝对精神不过是自哲学诞生以来一切哲学中人类中心主义狂妄的顶点，实质上是普遍利己主义者的概念。
人类中心主义也根植于费尔巴哈的唯物主义中，而正是这一点使它成为唯心主义——事实上，一切以主体性为中心的思想，即以人类主体性为中心的思想，归根结底都是唯心主义。
正因如此，马克思认为哲学历来都是唯心主义的，因此他提议通过采取第三方视角来摆脱哲学，把哲学转变为科学。因此，在马克思看来，科学的前提是放弃以主体性为中心的思想，并模仿第三方的（想象中的）视角。
当代哲学——与“分析哲学”（据称占据真正哲学的霸权地位）相对的“大陆哲学”——尤其是批判理论，鄙视经验主义。它对技术感兴趣，只是为了理论化其社会效果
；对理论数学好奇（例如前述新理性主义者），但可量化性、通过经验归纳进行的证明，却遭到隐晦蔑视。正是这种对物质（证明）的蔑视，使它至今仍是哲学，与巴门尼德和柏拉图式的“身体恐惧”叙事并无二致，即使它选择以其他名称自称（理论、后哲学等）。
en: Philosophy has always been anthropocentric, from antiquity to this day: in his ‘Critique of Hegel’s Philosophy in General’ (part of the
), Marx explains that the Absolute Spirit is simply the apex of the anthropocentric pretensions of all philosophy since its inception, amounting to the notion of the universal egoist.

Anthropocentrism is embedded in Feuerbach’s materialism too, and that is what renders it idealism – in fact, all subjectivity-centred thought – amounting to human-subjectivity-centred thought – comes down to idealism.

It is for this reason that, according to Marx, philosophy has always been idealist, and he thus proposes an exit from it by virtue of assuming the third party’s perspective, transforming philosophy into science. Therefore, in Marx, science is premised on the abandonment of subjectivity-centred thought and miming the third party’s (imagined) perspective.

Contemporary philosophy, the kind one calls ‘continental philosophy’ as opposed to ‘analytic philosophy’ (supposedly occupying the hegemonic position of philosophy proper), and critical theory in particular, despises empiricism. It displays interest in technology to simply theorize its social effects

and curiosity about theoretical mathematics (such as among the aforementioned neorationalists), but quantifiability, proof executed through empirical induction, is subject to tacit contempt. The contempt for the material (proof) is what makes it philosophy to this day, not much unlike the Parmenidean and Platonic somatophobic narratives, even when it chooses to call itself differently (theory, post-philosophy etc.).

zh: 进入21 世纪后，那种源自笛卡尔和柏拉图主义对物理事物的蔑视，仍在思辨现实主义启发的新理性主义、加速主义以及后人类主义网络理论中隐含或明示；这些理论往往不过是变相的超人类主义，也包括异质女性主义（xenofeminism）。身体和物理事物也属于运动、变化和衰败的范畴，被视为应予废除的幻象，以便纯粹理智——黑格尔的精神——以人工智能和人机奇点形式统治。自前苏格拉底哲学以来，讨论变得更精致复杂，但其根基似乎仍是同样的关切，因为若移除这些奠基前提，整个哲学大厦就会崩塌：存在是核心概念，本体论是哲学的归宿，形式理性与本体论一致，从而产生形而上学；而对物质世界及其应用的研究则被视为次要，正如“可见世界”一样。
en: Well into the twenty-first century, the old Cartesian and Platonist contempt for the physical is also implied or declared, as one can note in the speculative-realism-inspired neorationalism, accelerationism and posthumanist cyber theory that more often than not amounts to simply transhumanist but also xenofeminism Body, and the physical, is also of the register of movement, change and decay, and it is an illusion to be abolished so that pure Intellect – Hegel’s Spirit – would rule in the form of AI and machine-human singularity. Discussions have become more elaborate and more complex since the times of pre-Socratic philosophy, but they seem to be underpinned by the same concerns since the founding premises cannot be removed without the whole edifice falling apart: Being is the central notion, ontology is what philosophy comes down to, formal reason is aligned with ontology and thus produces metaphysics and the study of the material world and its application is of inferior importance, as is the ‘visible world’.

zh: “无中不能生有”——或存在来自存在——这一原则在科学探索中有意义，尤其在物理学（牛顿、霍金等）和化学中；这无需任何曲折的悖论和矛盾论证，不像埃利亚学派主张导致的困境。亚里士多德用其范畴论和逻辑揭示了埃利亚学派主张的不一致，从而证明将人类推理（范畴应用）与存在本身混同是一种谬误。通过把ousia 与质量、数量、位置和时间区分开，亚里士多德证明谓述总是关于某种特定事物；由于可能的谓述实际上无穷无尽，因此也存在多种ousia：“简言之，存在总是以复数形式被述说”［τὸ ὂν τὸ ἁπλῶς λεγόμενον λέγεται πολλαχῶς］（亚里士多德，《形而上学》E.2 1026a33–34）。作为这一论证的一部分，亚里士多德考察了人类思维运作、言语方式以及唯一可能可信且合乎逻辑的言语模式中可能存在的矛盾、不一致和悖论——而不是存在本身中的矛盾。这是与整个巴门尼德之后传统的革命性决裂：它从言语的逻辑一致性出发，即人类能够控制和完善的部分，而不是从存在本身出发。人类语言反映现实和外部世界的一致性，但后者本身似乎是封闭的，只有我们的范畴体系和逻辑发展到一定程度时才可理解。如果撞上矛盾之墙，那是人类推理的问题，而不是存在、外部世界或本质超出人类思维的现实的问题。在《物理学》中，亚里士多德写道：
en: Nothing comes from nothing – or being becomes out of being – is a principle that makes sense in scientific explorations, in particular in physics (Newton, Hawking etc.) and in chemistry, and this is possible without any convoluted affirmations of paradoxes and contradictions, unlike the

to which the Eleatic proposal led. Aristotle divulges the inconsistencies of the Eleatic proposal in terms of his categories and logic and thus demonstrates that the collapse of human reasoning (application of categories) and being itself is a fallacy. By distinguishing

from quality, quantity, location and time, Aristotle demonstrates that predication is always about a certain something, and as there is a practically endless or unbound multiplicity of possible predications, there is thus a multiplicity of

: ‘the being, put simply, is always said in plural’ [τὸ ὂν τὸ ἁπλῶς λεγόμενον λέγεται πολλαχῶς] (Aristotle, Meta. E.2 1026a33–34). As part of the elaboration of this argument, Aristotle examines possible contradictions, inconsistencies and paradoxes in how the human mind might work, or in the way one speaks and in the only possibly credible modes of speech that make sense – not in Being itself. This is a revolutionary break from the entire post-Parmenidean tradition – one which departs from the logical consistency of speech, that which is within the reach of human control and perfection, not from ‘Being itself’. Human language reflects the consistency of reality and the outside world, but the latter seems to be in and of itself foreclosed and accessible only to the degree to which our categorical system and logic are developed. If one runs against the wall of contradiction, it is due to a problem in human reasoning, not a problem of Being, of the outside world, of the real whose essence evades human mind. In

zh: 人们不容易把运动和变化归入另一个属（genus）——只要看看有些人把它归入何处就清楚了：他们把运动等同于差异、不等或非存在；但这些东西并不必然运动，无论它们不同、不等还是不存在。（201b19–201b23）
en: One could not easily put motion and change in another genus — this is plain if we consider where some people put it: they identify motion with difference or inequality or not being; but such things are not necessarily moved, whether they are different or unequal or non-existent. (201b19–201b23)

en: Furthermore, he argues:

zh: 因此，有人说虚空是物体的质料（他们也把位置等同于它），这种说法不正确；因为质料并不与事物分离，而他们却把虚空当作某种分离的东西来探究。（214a12–214a16）
en: So some say that the void is the matter of the body (they identify the place, too, with this), and in this they speak incorrectly; for the matter is not separable from the things, but they are inquiring about the void as about something separable. (214a12–214a16)

zh: 除了作为抽象范畴，人们不能把一般物质说成一个独立的存在者，正如也不能这样谈论虚空。因此，亚里士多德以“人们这样说是错误的”为理由驳斥了埃利亚学派的不可能性。亚里士多德考察了“organon”（理性推理及其规则的工具）及其在当时的可能性和局限，以便使对存在者（to on）以及非存在者的说明成为可能。所谓“非存在者”不是对存在的否定，而是对某种特定ousia、对“某物”的否定。
en: Except as an abstract category, one cannot speak of matter in general as a distinct ontic entity, just as one cannot speak of the void in such fashion either. Thus, the Eleatic impossibility is refuted by Aristotle on the grounds of ‘one [thus] speaks incorrectly’. Aristotle examines the ‘organon’ (the instrumentarium of rational reasoning and its rules) and its possibilities and its shortcomings of the era in order to make the account of
(tò ōn), as well as of
not, possible. That ‘which is not’ is not a negation of Being but rather of a particular
, of a ‘some-thing’.

zh: 亚里士多德《物理学》的上述引文带有鲜明的唯物主义色彩：物质与“存在之物”——某物，或 tò tí，或 ousia——不可分离。因此，物体并不是能够“承载”或容纳虚空或空的空间的东西，不能像留基伯和德谟克利特所尝试的那样，借此既使运动成为可能，又避免反驳埃利亚学派。恰恰相反，亚里士多德确实进行了这种反驳。按照亚里士多德的说法，早期原子论者所提出的妥协是：“他们说元素是充实与虚空，并分别把它们称为存在与非存在”［στοιχεῖα μὲν τὸ πλῆρες καὶ τὸ κενὸν εἶναί φασι, λέγοντες τὸ μὲν ὂν τὸ δὲ μὴ ὄν］（亚里士多德，《形而上学》A.4 985b5–6）。
这是一种谬误，一种推理错误，而且极可能是一种本体论上的不可能性。我们在这里使用“极可能”，因为亚里士多德似乎并不认为：仅仅由于我们所能依靠的是认知工具（organon）的完善，外部世界就不可通达。非存在是相对于某种 ousia 而言的偶发、巧合，或更确切地说，偶然性（sumbebekos）；它可以是一种虚假，最后，也可以是一种潜能（即作为存在者现象的生成）。
正如质料依存于某种 ousia，存在因而是正确谓述与现实性的范畴。正确使用范畴，能够导向对实在或存在的正确说明。亚里士多德的方法可以与今天所谓的科学推理相比：证明的工具（organon）的完善，能够使我们对外部世界、实在或存在的说明更加准确。
en: The above quote from Aristotle’s
resonates as staunchly materialistic: matter and ‘what is’ – the some-thing, or
or

– are inalienable; therefore, bodies are not something that can ‘carry’ or contain the void or empty space, so that the possibility of movement is foregrounded while avoiding refutation of the Eleatic, as Leucippus and Democritus have attempted to do. Quite to the contrary, Aristotle engages in such refutation. The compromise the early atomists offered was, according to Aristotle, that ‘the elements are said to be full and empty, calling them either being or non-being’ [στοιχεῖα μὲν τὸ πλῆρες καὶ τὸ κενὸν εἶναί φασι, λέγοντες τὸ μὲν ὂν τὸ δὲ μὴ ὄν] (Aristotle,

This is a fallacy, an error in reasoning and most probably an ontological impossibility. We are using ‘most probably’ here as Aristotle does not seem to think that the outside is impenetrable just because what we can rely on is the perfection of our cognitive instruments, the
. Non-being is a matter of accident or coincidence or rather contingency (
) with regard to an
; it can be a falsity and, finally, a potentiality (of becoming, as an ontic phenomenon).
Just as matter is contingent on an

, Being is therefore a category of correct predication and actuality. Correct use of categories can lead to a correct explanation of the real or of Being. Aristotle’s approach is comparable to what one might today call scientific reasoning – the perfection of the
of demonstration leads to accuracy in one’s account of the outside world, of the real or Being.

zh: 尽管如此，亚里士多德仍是哲学家——存在一种最高ousia 的终极真理，凌驾于众多ousiai 之上；在此意义上，实在与真理建立统一，因为实在通过真理或纯粹沉思超越自身——作为包括可感世界在内的一切存在者的“第一推动者”，是noesis（理性/思想）。（亚里士多德，《形而上学》1072a30–32）
又见：“被欲求者和思想的对象推动运动而自身不动。它们是第一的，也是同一的。”（《形而上学》1072a26–27）尽管如此，亚里士多德关于第一推动者的观念，是他整个著作尤其是《形而上学》和《物理学》中对埃利亚学派论证最直接的反驳。基于这一立场，亚里士多德既可被视为唯物主义者，也可被视为推动唯物主义立场发展的人：运动是一切存在者的原因，因此一切存在都是运动。
en: Aristotle remains a philosopher nonetheless – there is an ultimate truth of the ultimate
, overarching the plurality of
, whereby real and truth establish unity insofar as the real transcends itself through truth or pure contemplation – the ‘prime mover’ of all existing, including the sensible world, is
(reason/ ing). (Aristotle, Meta. 1072a30-32)

Also: ‘the desired and that which is subject of thought move while remaining unmoved. They are the first [primary] and the same’ (Meta. 1072a26-27) In spite of this, Aristotle’s notion of the prime mover is the most direct opposition to the Eleatic argument to be elaborated throughout his oeuvre, and primarily in
and

. By virtue of that stance, Aristotle can be considered either a materialist or working in favour of a development of a materialist position: movement is the cause of all existent, consequently, all existence is movement.

zh: 亚里士多德的哲学，或其唯物主义变体，站在前苏格拉底哲学家尤其是原子论者的肩上。
en: Aristotle’s philosophy, or its materialist variant, stands on the shoulders of the pre-Socratics, in particular the atomists.

zh: 原子论者

如前所述，巴门尼德禁止对虚无、非存在进行哲学说明，意味着不可能说明运动和变化。许多前苏格拉底哲学家试图在遵守巴门尼德“禁止非存在”的前提下，构想一种能够说明变化和运动的认识论可能性。原子论者德谟克利特和留基伯遵守巴门尼德公理：“存在来自存在”，“非存在来自非存在”，因此本体论上不存在非存在。尽管如此，他们找到一种绕过这一哲学困境的方法，以构建一种允许变化和运动的物理世界说明。显然，感官世界中可见的生长与衰败、出现与消失、空间位移中的运动，促使原子论者揭示现象背后的隐藏原理，并给出哲学解释。他们的解释显然是唯物主义的——它以物理学（physike）即自然哲学的形式表述。在早期原子论者时代以及整个古希腊，哲学一词涵盖科学或对周围现实的科学解释方法：经验观察被形式化，自然和存在的抽象与规律既从经验洞见中提炼，也被经验洞见证实。
en: Parmenides’ prohibition on a philosophical account of nothingness, non-being, as already noted, implied the impossibility of offering an account of movement and change. Many of the pre-Socratics have sought to conceptualize an epistemic possibility for giving an account of change and movement while observing Parmenides’ ‘ban on non-being’. The atomists, Democritus and Leucippus, adhere to the Parmenidean axiom, according to which ‘being comes from being’, whereas ‘non-being comes from non-being’, and there is therefore no such thing as non-being, ontologically speaking. Nonetheless, they have found a way around this philosophical

in order to create an account of the physical world that allows for change and movement. Obviously, what was visible in the sensible world, such as growth and decay, emergence and disappearance and movement through space displacement, urged the atomists to unravel the hidden principles of the phenomena and offer a philosophical explication of it. Their explication was, apparently, materialist – it was formulated in terms of physics, or
, a
of nature. In the time of the early atomists and throughout the period of Greek Antiquity, the word

encompassed sciences or the scientific approach to the explication of the surrounding reality: empirical observations were formalized, and abstractions and laws of nature and Being were extracted from such empirical insights as well as corroborated by them.

zh: 有限性——存在之坚实与完满不可或缺的条件

children: Finitude – the indispensable condition for the solidity and fullness of being

zh: 存在确实不可分割，芝诺悖论被颠倒过来：遵循埃利亚原则，我们只能断言，必然存在某种存在实例，其分割不可能，如果我们遵守“无中不能生有”原则。也就是说，存在一个a-tomos 点，一个确实坚实、不变、永恒的自然元素——原子，即“不可分割者”（DK 67A7，DK 68A37）。在《论生成与消灭》（325b12–325b33）中，亚里士多德论证，原子论者设定不可分割物体的动机，是为埃利亚学派提出的运动、变化和多样性（不）可能性悖论提供答案。
en: Being is indeed indivisible, and Zeno’s paradox is reversed: by observing the Eleatic principle, we can only claim that there must be an instance of Being where its division becomes impossible if we are to observe the principle of ‘nothing comes from nothing’. Namely, there is a point of a-tomos, an element of nature that is indeed solid, unchangeable and permanent – the
, the ‘indivisible’ (DK 67A7, DK 68A37). In
(325b12– 325b33), Aristotle argues that the motivation for the atomists’ postulation of indivisible bodies was to proffer an answer to the
brought forth by the Eleatics, namely that of the (im)possibility of movement, change and multiplicity.

zh: 因此，正是通过遵守埃利亚原则，原子论者才达到一个允许设想多样性和运动的实例。这就是不可分割（“不可切割”）、现实化的物质之点——atomos。（亚里士多德，《物理学》206a14–206a18）如果空间确实被视为无限可分，那么存在之坚实、稳定和固定的论证就会被削弱甚至完全矛盾。因此，埃利亚立场在术语上就是矛盾的——它试图证明万物始终如其所是、不变且不可变，却否定了变化可能，从而否定了运动。这隐含着无限。
en: Thus, by observing precisely the Eleatic principle, the atomists have reached an instance that allows for the conceiving of multiplicity and movement. That is the point of an indivisible (‘uncuttable’), actualized matter –
. (Aristotle,

. 206a14–206a18) If space should indeed be considered subject to limitless divisibility, the argument for solidity, stability and fixity of Being would be undermined if not contradicted entirely. Therefore, the Eleatic position is one of contradiction in terms – by seeking to demonstrate that everything has ever existed as it is, unchanging and unchangeable, it rejects the possibility of change and thus movement. Infinity is implied.

zh: 所有这一切都以“无中不能生有”原则为依据。然而，正因接受“无中不能生有”，原子论者才证明变化不仅可能而且必然，因为有限性实际上是其前提——无限意味着可分，无限可分意味着任何形式的坚实和完满存在都不可能。古典埃利亚论证是本体论的，因为它依赖把存在物化为抽象的形式论证。然而，原子论者的论证属于自然哲学：对自然（physis）的一种以经验为基础的说明——物质的无限分割或切割意味着，在physis 的核心，否定或消灭行为愈发在场且压倒性。引入atomos 点，即不可切割、不可分割者，就是确认一种超越毁灭的物质现实实例和形式。因此，有限性保证了“无中不能生有”原则得到遵守。这种立场由原子论者阐述，但毕达哥拉斯学派似乎在原子论者之前就持有类似观点。
en: All of this is justified by the principle of ‘nothing comes from nothing’. However, by endorsing the principle of ‘nothing comes from nothing’, the atomists have proven that change is not only possible but necessary, as finitude is actually its prerequisite – infinity implies divisibility, and infinite divisibility implies the impossibility of solidity and fullness of being of any sort. The classical Eleatic argument is ontological, as it relies on a formal argument of the being as reified abstraction. The argument of the atomists, however, is that of the natural philosophy: an empirically grounded account of
– infinite division or cutting of matter implies an ever more present and overwhelming presence of the act of introducing negation or annihilation at the heart of
. Introducing a point of

, or of the uncuttable, of the indivisible, is the identification of an instance and form of material reality that is beyond destruction. Thus, finitude is what vouches for the observance of the principle ‘nothing comes from nothing’. Such a position is elaborated by the atomists, but it seems that the Pythagoreans held a similar stance prior to the atomists.

zh: 亚里士多德进一步为原子论立场提供佐证，他论证道：
en: Aristotle offers further corroboration of the atomist stance by arguing:

zh: 事物既被认为潜能地存在，也被认为现实地存在。此外，事物要么通过增加，要么通过分割而无限。正如我们所见，大小并非现实无限。但通过分割，它是无限的。（驳斥不可分割线的理论并不困难。）那么剩下的选择是：无限具有潜在存在。但我们不能像说“这可能是一尊雕像”那样理解潜在存在——这会是一尊雕像，但无限不会现实存在。存在以多种方式被述说，我们说无限存在，其意义如同我们说“现在是白天”或“现在是竞技会”，因为事物总是一个接一个地产生。（《物理学》206a14–206a25）
en: Now things are said to exist both potentially and in fulfilment. Further, a thing is infinite either by addition or by division. Now, as we have seen, magnitude is not actually infinite. But by division it is infinite. (There is no difficulty in refuting the theory of indivisible lines.) The alternative then remains that the infinite has a potential existence. But we must not construe potential existence in the way we do when we say that it is possible for this to be a statue—this will be a statue, but something infinite will not be in actuality. Being is spoken of in many ways, and we say that the infinite is in the sense in which we say it is day or it is the games, because one thing after another is always coming into existence. (

zh: 由否定性或“空无物质”促成的运动与变化

children: Movement and change enabled by negative or ‘empty matter’

zh: 亚里士多德在说明早期原子论者时写道：“元素或者是充实的，或者是空的，也可以分别称为存在或非存在”；原文为：“στοιχεῖα μὲν τὸ πλῆρες καὶ τὸ κενὸν εἶναί φασι, λέγοντες τὸ μὲν ὂν τὸ δὲ μὴ ὄν.”（《形而上学》A.4 985b5–6）这样，“非存在”就参与存在，因为它的在场是对构成物质的原子的掏空——kenosis。因此，虚无参与存在，却不是存在的起源；它毋宁嵌在主要被视为物质或自然（physis）的存在的核心之中。原子论者必须提出两个论点：存在是多重的，而空或虚空——空间的缺失，或任何东西的缺失——是物质现实的一个方面。这是在试图克服一种困境：遵守埃利亚法则，阻碍了对运动、变化、生成和衰亡问题的科学与哲学考察。这一尝试类似赫拉克利特的解决办法：“一”实际上是多；即使它几乎熄灭，也不会彻底熄灭，而会“按照一定的尺度”重新燃起，也就是遵循自然与存在的内在法则，亦即科学与本体论的法则。（DK22B30）原文为：κόσμον τόνδε, τὸν αὐτὸν ἁπάντων, οὔτε τις θεῶν οὔτε ἀνθρώπων ἐποίησεν, ἀλλ’ ἦν ἀεὶ καὶ ἔστιν καὶ ἔσται πῦρ ἀείζωον, ἁπτόμενον μέτρα καὶ ἀποσβεννύμενον μέτρα（DK22B30）。赫拉克利特假定存在几乎完全熄灭；与之不同，原子论者谈论的是原子内部的绝对虚空。
en: ‘The elements are either full or empty, or they could be called either being or non-being’, explains Aristotle in his account of the early atomists; or, in the original: ‘στοιχεῖα μὲν τὸ πλῆρες καὶ τὸ κενὸν εἶναί φασι, λέγοντες τὸ μὲν ὂν τὸ δὲ μὴ ὄν.’ (
. A.4 985b5-6) In this way, ‘non-being’ participates in Being as its presence is a hollowing out –
– of the atoms that constitute matter. Therefore, nothingness participates in Being without being its origin and is rather nested at the heart of Being seen primarily as matter or

. The atomists had to put forward the thesis that Being is multiple as well as the thesis that emptiness or void (the absence of space or of anything for that matter) is an aspect of material reality. This attempt to overcome the frustration of scientific and philosophical examination of the question of movement, change, generation and degeneration, created by the observance of the Eleatic law, resembles Heraclites’s solution: the One is in fact multiple, and even though it might go virtually extinguished, it never fully goes out, instead rekindling ‘according to certain measures’, that is, internal laws of nature and Being, scientific and ontological. (DK22B30) Or, in the original: κόσμον τόνδε, τὸν αὐτὸν ἁπάντων, οὔτε τις θεῶν οὔτε ἀνθρώπων ἐποίησεν, ἀλλ’ ἦν ἀεὶ καὶ ἔστιν καὶ ἔσται πῦρ ἀείζωον, ἁπτόμενον μέτρα καὶ ἀποσβεννύμενον μέτρα (DK22B30). Unlike Heraclitus, who assumes a virtual extinction of existence, the atomists speak of an absolute void inside of an atom.

zh: 希腊哲学中理解运动的困难——并不只见于前苏格拉底思想家——在于它对运动的本体论定义：运动是存在与生成的问题，是从一种 ousia 转变为另一种 ousia。从纯粹本体论上说，这种运动似乎不可能，而且确实涉及存在从非存在中产生这一前提。存在过去存在、现在存在，而且将永远存在；生成是不可能的。运动很少被同空间、自然哲学，或关于物质行为的精确推理联系起来。即使前苏格拉底思想家，尤其是原子论者，确实建立了这种联系，空的空间也成为非存在的一种可能性，存在的充实与无限在场因而受到损害。梅利索斯认为，“空”——显然被理解为一个空间范畴——就是无：“因为虚空就是无”，原文为 τὸ γὰρ κενεὸν οὐδέν ἐστιν（DK 30B7.7）。为了使某物生成，就必须假定此前没有这种 ousia；为了使一种 ousia“位移”，便必须设想空间被腾空，它又在一个此前绝对空无的空间中重新出现；而那个空间被理解为非存在。亚里士多德在《物理学》中记述了原子论者对运动的这种理解：“这些人认为，虚空是一道间隙，非存在以可感物体的方式在其中存在。”（《物理学》IV.6 213a27–9）希腊文底本为：οἱ δὲ ἄνθρωποι βούλονται κενὸν εἶναι διάστημα ἐν ᾧ μηδέν ἐστι σῶμα ἰσθητόν。
en: The trouble with conceiving movement in Greek philosophy, and not only among the pre-Socratics, lies in its ontological definition – it is a matter of Being and becoming, of movement from one

into another. Speaking purely ontologically, such movement seems impossible and does involve the premise of the emergence of Being from non-being. Being has been, is and will always be – becoming is an impossibility. It is rarely linked with space and natural philosophy or exact reasoning concerning the behaviour of matter. With the pre-Socratics, and the atomists more specifically, even when it is, empty space becomes a possibility for non-being, and the fullness and limitless being-there of Being is compromised. Melissus argues that ‘the empty’, apparently conceived as a spatial category, is nothing: ‘as the empty is nothing’, or, in the original, τὸ γὰρ κενεὸν οὐδέν ἐστιν (DK 30B7.7). In order for something to become, the previous absence of
is assumed; in order for an

to ‘displace’ itself, one ought to imagine an evacuation of space and re-emergence in an absolutely empty prior space which is understood as non-being. This understanding of movement among the atomists is noted by Aristotle in his
: ‘these people reasoned that the empty is a fissure through which non-being is in the way of a sensible body’ (
IV.6 213a27-9 ), or, in the Greek original: οἱ δὲ ἄνθρωποι βούλονται κενὸν εἶναι διάστημα ἐν ᾧ μηδέν ἐστι σῶμα ἰσθητόν.
body.review: 这里的中文引句依本书英文释义译出。书中所附希腊文的句意为“人们认为虚空是其中没有可感物体的间隔”，与其英文释义不完全相合；底本希腊词形 ἰσθητόν 照录，不静默改写。

zh: 亚里士多德最早把空间，从而把运动，归入可以作为谓词一部分但不参与“本质”或“实体”即ousia 的范畴。这样，亚里士多德既在本体论上，也在自然哲学上提供了解决方案，允许对运动这一物质现象进行精确和数学的探索。
en: Aristotle was the first to place space, and therefore movement, among the categories that can become a part of a predicate but do not participate in the ‘essences’ or ‘substances’, that is,
. In this way, Aristotle offers a solution both ontological as well as in terms of natural philosophy, allowing for exact and mathematical explorations of the material phenomenon of movement.

伊壁鸠鲁派无需假设“原子包含虚空”便能解释运动与变化：原子是“坚实的”物质，而生长与衰亡遵循物质保存的法则：
en: Or in English translation: ‘Would space be needed for the growth of things; Were life an increment of nothing: then; The tiny babe forthwith would walk a man, And from the turf would leap a branching tree — Wonders unheard of; for, by Nature, each; Slowly increases from its lawful seed, And through that increase shall conserve its kind’.

The Epicureans did not need the conjecture of ‘atoms containing void’ in order to proffer an account of movement and change – atoms are ‘solid’ matter, and growth and decay observe the laws of its preservation:

为了使物质在其有限或受限却无界的存在中不断运动与生长

en: Or in English translation: ‘Thus primal bodies are solid, without a void.; But since there’s void in all begotten things; All solid matter must be round the same; Nor, by true reason canst thou prove aught hides; And holds a void within its body, unless; Thou grant what holds it be a solid. Know; That which can hold a void of things within; Can be naught else than matter in union knit’.
For the matter to constantly move and grow within its finite or limited yet unbound existence

– ‘as there is nothing beyond existence, it is naught and therefore it is not to be found outside the realm of material reality – space is required and nothingness contained within the material universe: Such huge abundance spreads for things around— / Room off to every quarter, without end. Lastly, before our very eyes is seen / Thing to bound thing: air hedges hill from hill, / And mountain walls hedge air; land ends the sea, / And sea in turn all lands / but for the All / Truly is nothing which outside may bound’.

The swerve appears at an uncertain time and location – in the original, ‘incerto tempore ferme incertisque locis spatio deflectere paulum’ (Lucretius Carus, Liber II, 219–20) – which then causes collision, dispersion and reorganization in the atomic linkages, one structure falling apart and a new one emerging. Movement is constant, as the absoluteness of the void does not allow for the atoms to stand still – there is no location that they could occupy in the void that is empty in an absolute way, disallowing position, as it does not create any opposition, resistance or matter that would constitute such supposed location.

zh: 虚空实际上是虚无，是绝对的无，因此它只在概念上存在，而非本体论上——毋宁说，面对虚空的毁灭力量，生命以及只能以物理形式存在的存在不断诞生并重生。空间和位置没有物理表征，它们是无界且纯粹延展：“空间无边界也无尺度，向四面八方无量延伸。”（卢克莱修·卡鲁斯，《物性论》II, 91–2）原文：“quoniamspatium sine fine modoquest, inmensumque patere in cunctas undique partis”。空间无法度量，表明它被理解为虚空的一个方面，以及那种使变化成为可能、却不产生任何东西的虚无——“无中不能生有”是原子论原则。然而，它是一个能够让我们把握变化和运动的范畴。毁灭潜能是物质本身固有的，是原子行为的一个方面，而正是这种否定性维持生命。但它本身并不构成本体论现实——无即不存在之物，它只存在于原子碰撞的缝隙中，存在于除此以外皆为坚实物质的原子之间。卢克莱修·卡鲁斯用以下比喻解释空间（就虚空而言）在物质（物理）过程发生中的作用：
en: The void is in fact nothingness, an absolute naught, and it therefore exists only conceptually, not ontologically – it is rather that against the annihilating power of the void life and thus existence that could be found only in a physical form are born and perpetually reborn. Space and location do not have a physical representation, they are unbound and pure extension: ‘Space has no bound nor measure, and extends; Unmetered forth in all directions round. (Titus Lucretius Carus,

en: , 91–2) Or in the original: ‘quoniam spatium sine fine modoquest, inmensumque patere in cunctas undique partis’. The fact that space has no measure points to its understanding as an aspect of the void and of that enabling nothingness that does not engender anything – ‘nothing comes from nothing’ is the atomist principle. Yet it is a category that enables change and movement to be grasped. The potentiality of annihilation is intrinsic to matter itself, and an aspect of the behaviour of the atoms and that very negativity is what sustains life. However, it does not constitute an ontological reality in and of itself – nothing is what is not, and it exists only in the fissures of collisions of atoms, amidst the otherwise solid matter the atoms are. Lucretius Carus uses the following metaphors to explain the role of space (with regard to void) in the occurrence of material (physical) processes:

zh: 在光线所照的虚空中，它们不断战斗，仿佛永恒争斗；成队交锋，毫不停歇，在相遇与分离中上下奔忙。由此你便可推想，原初种子在更大的虚空中不停颠簸，究竟是怎样的情形——至少在这限度之内。（卢克莱修·卡鲁斯，第2卷，118–123）

From this thou mayest conjecture of what sort; The ceaseless tossing of primordial seeds; Amid the mightier void – at least so far. (Lucretius Carus, Liber II, 118–23)

zh: 虚无是一个本体论概念，但不是一种作为存在者的实在。然而，它引发曲线、偏转或clinamen，因此不只是抽象。就其作为原子碰撞导致的衰败和毁灭过程的效果而言，它是真实的。然而，从因果上看，偏转先于碰撞，是虚空本身的属性。再者，虚空在空间上不存在，也没有时间固定点。人们或许会猜想，它是原子运动的属性，不构成时间因果性，而后者本身并非线性。虚空存在，是因为原子必须碰撞；它们碰撞，是因为不存在有中心、能保证静态位置的空间虚空。在这个意义上，虚空缺席于物质和原子的构成，却又作为“运算子”出现在永不停息的原子组合与分解活动中。人们可以把它比作今天所说的反粒子，或空间测量的抽象范畴，因为它既能引发产生存在的偏转和碰撞，又只是概念，没有事实上的、时间的或空间的位置，也没有物质实体，尽管它对原子现实产生物质效果。
en: Nothingness is an ontological concept but not an ontic reality. Yet it occasions the curve, or the swerve or

, and thus it is not only an abstraction. It is real insofar as it is an effect of processes of decay and destruction that occur due to the atoms’ collisions. However, causally, the swerve precedes the collisions and is a property of the void itself. Yet again, the void does not exist spatially, nor does it have temporal fixed point. One might conjure that it is the property of atoms’ movement and does not constitute temporal causality whereas the latter is not linear. The void is there because atoms must collide, and they do so as there is no spatial void with a centre that can ensure a static position. In that sense, the void is absent from matter and the constitution of atoms and yet again makes itself present as an ‘operator’ in the never-ceasing atomic actions of composition and decomposition. One might liken it to what is nowadays known as anti-particles or the abstract category of measurement of space, since it has the capacity to cause the swerve and the collision that engenders existence while being mere concept without factual, temporal and special position or body of matter, albeit with a material effect on the atomic reality.

zh: 拉丁文原文：Praeterea si iam finitum constituatur; omne quod est spatium, si quis procurrat ad oras; ultimus extremas iaciatque uolatile telum; (I, 970) id ualidis utrum contortum uribus ire; quo fuerit missum mauis longeque uolare; an prohibere aliquid censes obstareque posse?; alterutrum fatearis enim sumasque necessest.; quorum utrumque tibi effugium praecludit et omne; cogit ut exempta concedas fine patere; nam siue est aliquid quod probeat officiatque; quominus quo missum est ueniat finique locet se; siue foras fertur, non est a fine profectum. ; (I, 980) hoc pacto sequar atque, oras ubicumque locaris; extremas, quaeram: quid telo denique fiet?; fiet uti nusquam possit consistere finis; effugiumque fugae prolatet copia semper; Praeterea spatium summai totius omne; (I 984) undique si inclusum certis consisteret oris; finitumque foret, iam copia materiai; undique ponderibus solidis confluxet ad imum; nec res ulla geri sub caeli tegmine posset; nec foret omnino caelum neque lumina solis; quippe ubi materies omnis cumulata iaceret (I, 990); ex infinito iam tempore subsidendo. 991(Liber I, 970–90)。至于英文，这里破例使用 Martin Ferguson Smith 的译文，因为它更便于同拉丁原文逐行对照：“再假定一切现存的空间是有限的，有人跑到其最远边缘，将一支矛掷出去：你认为这支用强劲力量掷出的矛会远飞并抵达目标，还是认为会有什么东西挡住它的去路，使它停下？你必须认可并选择这两种假设中的一种，但二者都会堵住你的退路，迫使你承认宇宙的广延是无限的。因为，无论有什么东西挡住长矛，使它无法击中并留在目标上，还是它继续飞行，它都不是从宇宙的尽头出发的。我就这样紧追着你：无论你把最远边界设在哪里，我都会追问长矛最终怎样了。我们的结论是，任何地方都不能固定一条边界；面对飞行的无限可能性，永远无从逃避。”（第1卷，968–991）引自 Lucretius：《物性论》（On the Nature of Things），Martin Ferguson Smith 译并作导论与注释（Hackett Publishing Company，1969）。
en: In the Latin original: Praeterea si iam finitum constituatur; omne quod est spatium, si quis procurrat ad oras; ultimus extremas iaciatque uolatile telum; (I, 970) id ualidis utrum contortum uribus ire; quo fuerit missum mauis longeque uolare; an prohibere aliquid censes obstareque posse?; alterutrum fatearis enim sumasque necessest.; quorum utrumque tibi effugium praecludit et omne; cogit ut exempta concedas fine patere; nam siue est aliquid quod probeat officiatque; quominus quo missum est ueniat finique locet se; siue foras fertur, non est a fine profectum. ; (I, 980) hoc pacto sequar atque, oras ubicumque locaris; extremas, quaeram: quid telo denique fiet?; fiet uti nusquam possit consistere finis; effugiumque fugae prolatet copia semper; Praeterea spatium summai totius omne; (I 984) undique si inclusum certis consisteret oris; finitumque foret, iam copia materiai; undique ponderibus solidis confluxet ad imum; nec res ulla geri sub caeli tegmine posset; nec foret omnino caelum neque lumina solis; quippe ubi materies omnis cumulata iaceret (I, 990); ex infinito iam tempore subsidendo. 991(Liber I, 970–90), or in English, let’s, as an exception, use Martin Ferguson Smith’s translation as it’s easier to follow the alignment with the Latin original: ‘Then again, just suppose that all the existing space were finite, and that someone ran forward to the edge of its farthest border and launched a spear into flight: do you favour the view that the spear, cast with virile vigor, would fly far and reach its target, or do you suppose that something could check it by obstructing its course? You must grant and adopt one or the other of these hypotheses, and yet both deny you a subterfuge and compel you to acknowledge that the expanse of the universe is infinite. For whether there is something to check the spear and prevent it from hitting its mark and lodging in its target, or whether it flies on, it did not start from the end of the universe. In this way I will dog you: wherever you locate the farthest border, I will ask about the ultimate fate of the spear. Our conclusion will be that nowhere can a boundary be fixed: no escape will ever be-found from the limitless possibility of flight (Liber I, 968–91), from Lucretius,
, translated with Introduction and Notes by Martin Ferguson Smith (Hackett Publishing Company, 1969).
